# Questions only a person can answer

> 47 questions. 14 of them stand between the site and taking money, and say so.
>
> Nothing here is an answer. Each says why it matters, who to ask and where the question came from.
>
> This is the starting draft that ships with the back end, as it was written. The copy people work from is in the back end, under [Plans, Questions](https://quickpickle.vercel.app/backstage/plans/questions), and may have been changed there since. This file does not follow those changes.

## Product facts

### Where is it made, and by whom: you, or someone making it for you?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** It decides which food plan applies and who registers, whose name and address go on the label, and whether anything can be said about where it is from.
- **Where it came from:** To-do list; questions for Ashleigh 12

### What is in it? The ingredients list and the nutrition panel, exactly as they will be printed on the label, and anything that has to be declared as an allergen.

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh, with whoever makes it
- **Why it matters:** The site says nothing about what is in the bottle until this is confirmed, and the label cannot be printed without it.
- **Where it came from:** Go-live list (ingredients); to-do list; questions for Ashleigh 12

### How long does it keep, how was that worked out, and how must it be stored before and after opening?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh, with whoever makes it
- **Why it matters:** The label needs a date mark and a storage line, and neither can be guessed. It also sets how big a batch can be and how long stock can sit.
- **Where it came from:** To-do list; questions for Ashleigh 12

### Is the business registered to sell food in New Zealand, and under which kind of food plan?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh, with MPI or the council
- **Why it matters:** Food cannot be sold without the right registration. MPI's online tool says which plan applies, and the answer depends on where and how it is made.
- **Where it came from:** Compliance checklist

### Who checks the label before it is printed, and is "pickle juice shot" the right name for it on the pack?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** A reprint costs money, and a wrong label can mean bringing a batch back. The compliance checklist lists what to check.
- **Where it came from:** Questions for Ashleigh 9

### Is there one juice, or is more than one flavour planned?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** The site sells one juice in three pack sizes. A second flavour changes the label, the stock and the page.
- **Where it came from:** Questions for Ashleigh 10

### When will there be a finished bottle, with its real label, to photograph?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** The site shows a drawing of the bottle. One straight-on photo on plain card replaces it.
- **Where it came from:** To-do list

## The offer

### What are the pack sizes, their names and their prices?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** Packs of 6, 12 and 24 are planned, but the names and prices on the site are stand-ins. Set them once the Budget shows what a pack costs.
- **Where it came from:** Go-live list (packs); to-do list; questions for Ashleigh 11

### Does it launch as a pre-order for a first batch, or with stock on the shelf? If it is a pre-order, what date does the first batch ship from?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** The site is set up as a pre-order. A pre-order with no ship date is not something to take money for.
- **Where it came from:** Go-live list (ship-date); to-do list; questions for Ashleigh 15

### Which courier, where do we deliver, and what does it cost us and the customer?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** A courier, for a quote
- **Why it matters:** The delivery prices on the site are stand-ins, and so is delivering anywhere in New Zealand. It needs a courier's quote for a small box of liquid, rural included.
- **Where it came from:** Go-live list (shipping-rates); to-do list

### Have you read the delivery, returns, terms and privacy pages on the site, and do you agree to what they promise?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Whoever runs the business side
- **Why it matters:** They promise a replacement or the money back if an order arrives damaged, and the money back on a pre-order cancelled before it ships. They are your promises to make.
- **Where it came from:** Go-live list (returns-promises); to-do list

### Are the stickers and any merchandise given away, or sold?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** If they are sold they are products, with prices and stock. If they are given away they are a cost on every order in the Budget.
- **Where it came from:** Questions for Ashleigh 17

## The business

### What is the legal entity behind the store: its name, its New Zealand Business Number and its address?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Whoever runs the business side
- **Why it matters:** The terms of sale name no seller yet, the label needs a name and address, and the bank and Stripe will both ask.
- **Where it came from:** Go-live list (legal-entity); to-do list; questions for Ashleigh 12

### Is the business registered for GST in New Zealand?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Whoever runs the business side
- **Why it matters:** Receipts cannot show GST until this is known, and the Budget works its sums both ways until it is. Nothing assumes either answer.
- **Where it came from:** Go-live list (legal-entity); to-do list

### Is there a Stripe account in the business's name, with a bank account for it to pay into?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Whoever runs the business side
- **Why it matters:** Stripe is the chosen way to take payment. Until its keys are connected the checkout charges nobody.
- **Where it came from:** To-do list

### What is the customer email address?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Whoever runs the business side
- **Why it matters:** The policies and the questions on the site leave a gap where it goes, and customers need somewhere to write.
- **Where it came from:** Go-live list (contact-email); to-do list

### What is the domain name?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Whoever runs the business side
- **Why it matters:** The customer email address and email in the back end both hang off it.
- **Where it came from:** To-do list

### Is Xero set up, and who is the accountant?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Whoever runs the business side
- **Why it matters:** Accounting is not done in the back end. The month-end sheet assumes Xero and an accountant.
- **Where it came from:** How-to sheets

## Making and sending

### How many shots are in the first batch, and when is production day?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** It sets the ship date, how much packaging to order and how much money is tied up before the first sale.
- **Where it came from:** Business plan

### Who supplies the juice or its ingredients, the bottles, caps, labels and cartons, and what does each cost?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** Every line on the Budget is a blank until there are real quotes. Lead times decide how early to order.
- **Where it came from:** Budget

### Who packs and sends orders, where is stock kept, and what box does each pack go in?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** The packing sheet has blanks for the box, the padding and where slips are filed.
- **Where it came from:** How-to sheets

### What does a packed box weigh, for each pack size, and how big is it?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** A courier charges by weight and size. The file the Courier screen makes for the courier's website leaves both out until they are known, so they are typed in on the courier's site each time.
- **Where it came from:** Courier screen

## The claim lines

### What happens to the lead line from the concept deck, the one that says what the product does and how fast?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** It cannot go on the site, the pack or an ad in New Zealand, because a food may not be sold on what it does to a body. The site is built without it. If anyone wants it back, that is a conversation with a food lawyer or MPI first. Until you say otherwise, it stays out.
- **Where it came from:** To-do list; questions for Ashleigh 21

### Who signs off anything that could be read as a claim about the product?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** No ad, pack or product page should go out without one named person having checked it. Today that is nobody.
- **Where it came from:** Questions for Ashleigh 20

### Two softer lines from the deck are also held back: the title with the word "performance" in it, and the one that ends "for the quads". Keep them out, or get advice on them? And what does "the quads" mean to you: a part of the leg, a name for your people, or both?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** Next to a food, both lean towards saying what it does. If the quads is a name for your people it could be used that way. If it is a part of the body it stays out.
- **Where it came from:** To-do list; questions for Ashleigh 7 and 24

### Are you happy for your Meet Lucky story to run without the two sentences about the body holding a player back?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** On a page that sells the product they set up a claim, so the site leaves them out. They are your words, so it is your call to confirm.
- **Where it came from:** Questions for Ashleigh 22

### Lucky's full title in your file ends in "with Pickle Power". Are you happy with "Lucky, the superhero cat" until there is advice on it?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** Next to a food, the word power can read as a claim about what it gives you.
- **Where it came from:** Questions for Ashleigh 23

## Who it is for

### Who is it really for? Is "people with a game-day ritual" right, and which sports come first?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** Every word on the site assumes club and weekend players. If the real buyers are someone else, the words and the channels change.
- **Where it came from:** Questions for Ashleigh 6 and 8

### Beyond the website, what comes next: clubs and teams, events, shops? In what order?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** The marketing plan guesses clubs first, then events. Shops would need wholesale prices and another look at the label.
- **Where it came from:** Questions for Ashleigh 14

### Which clubs, events or stockists may we name in public, and is their permission in writing?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** Nobody is named without written permission on file. Today the answer is nobody.
- **Where it came from:** Questions for Ashleigh 16

### Do you want the small round of research run: eight to twelve chats with people who play, and a table at one event?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** Who it is for is a guess until someone is asked. This is the cheap way to check before money goes into packaging and ads.
- **Where it came from:** Questions for Ashleigh 18

### Which other pickle juice products, or anything like them, do you know of on sale in New Zealand?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** The brand pack's desk look found none made here, which may only mean they are not easy to find online.
- **Where it came from:** Questions for Ashleigh 19

### May we use te reo Māori greetings in replies and posts?

### One emoji at most in a caption, with the pickle allowed?

- **Who to ask:** Ashleigh
- **Why it matters:** The replies on the how-to sheets end with a name. Decide whose.
- **Where it came from:** Questions for Ashleigh 26

### Who watches the comments on our social pages, and do we hide ones that say what it did to someone's body?

## Site and hosting

### Has Quick Pickle finished moving to its own hosting and database accounts, and has the first owner sign-in been made?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Sam
- **Why it matters:** Real orders need a real database. Until one is connected the back end runs on made-up records and the shop cannot keep an order.
- **Where it came from:** To-do list; go-live list

### Vercel Pro, or move the hosting to Cloudflare?

- **In the way of launch:** yes
- **Who to ask:** Sam
- **Why it matters:** The free hosting plan is for personal projects, not a business's shop. One or the other has to be in place before the shop opens to the public. In November 2026 Vercel Pro was US$20 a month with nothing to move, and Cloudflare US$5 a month with the site moved and tested again.
- **Where it came from:** To-do list

### Is email set up for the business's own domain?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Sam
- **Why it matters:** Order emails, the inbox and the Pickle Crew emails all need it. The plan is Resend to start with, and it needs the domain first.
- **Where it came from:** To-do list

### Are the two access tokens in place, so the repository's own automation can run the database and the hosting?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Sam
- **Why it matters:** Without them those jobs are done by hand.
- **Where it came from:** To-do list

### Is anything left to do before the site opens to search?

- **In the way of launch:** no
- **Who to ask:** Sam
- **Why it matters:** It opens by itself once every stand-in fact on the go-live list is settled. One build check is switched back on at the same time.
- **Where it came from:** To-do list
